messages.subject: query from a newbie
parts:
Greetings from a newbie,

I am doing an MRes in DICE, University of Kent and I am very new to
the DISTANCE software and am trying to get the hang of it to process
my transect data. For this I have gone through the relevant chapters
of the Help menu of DISTANCE 6.0 and also key chapters of
"Introduction to Distance Sampling" by Buckland et al.

Before organizing my data in the right format in Excel, I would need
some inputs for the following situation:

- I have done a number of transects at 5 different study areas in a
given reserve
- For each study area I had between 2 and 4 transect lines
- Each transect line has a different length
- I walked one transect line per day and covered each transect line n
times with 1<n<5
- After completing the work at one study area, I moved to another one
- My observations are mostly arboreal mammals
- I wish to:
estimate the densities of the species for which I have adequate data
compare the densities for the various study areas
find out how the estimates would have been affect if I had covered
each transect less number of times
find out how the estimates would have been affected if I had cut less
transects at each study area

To start with I propose to open one DISTANCE project per study area
and work out my density estimates for the various species.

I assume that this can be done by preparing one data sheet per study
area comprising all observations and then using the filters in
Distance to calculate density estimates species wise. I would have the
following fields:

Stratum, Area, Transect, Distance, Length, Cluster size, Specie=
s

Is this correct?

When looking at the help file of DISTANCE as well as the book
"Introduction to Distance Sampling", I am not sure how to take care of
the fact that each transect line has been walked a variable number of
times. Should I just consider each occasion as a new transect and give
it a new name (Tr1, Tr2,Tr3,Tr4, etc), or should I club all occasions
of a given transect into a single transect name and then associate the
total length walked with that transect name?

I also notice the following statement in the help menu under chapter 5
section "Introduction to data import":
Notice also that all transects from the same stratum are grouped
together, and all observations from the same transect are grouped
together. If you accidentally forgot to sort the data before
importing it, so that for example the first four lines looked like
this:

Stratum A;100;Line 1A;10;14
Stratum A;100;Line 1A;10;8
Stratum A;100;Line 2A;10.3;7
Stratum A;100;Line 1A;10;22

then Distance would interpret this as three transects with labels
=93Line 1A=94, =93Line 2A=94 and =93Line 1A=94 again.

This appears at first look to be a possible way for me as the same
transect name could be used more than once when the transect gets
repeated. I would then associate the single length of the transect
with each entry.

A search in the discussion list with keywords "repeated transects" led
me to a few posting mentioning "pooling. Unfortunately I could not
find such references in the help menu or in the book ...

Any help to this newbie would be appreciated, even more that, like
many students, I feel crippled when I enter the world of statistics.

How would you suggest me to proceed? Thanks in advance

Regards to all
